deities: Lord Shiva as Tryambakeshwar (the 'three-eyed' lord; patron deity)
Idols of all Hindu gods and goddesses across the 13 floors (mini-shrines on each level)

history.dynasty: None (local tradition attributes foundation to Adi Shankaracharya; 13-storey structure is modern)
history.period: Tradition claims 8th-9th century (Adi Shankaracharya); one source says 12th century (conflicting - verify; the present 13-storey building is a modern construction)
history.summary: This is the 13-storey 'Tera Manzil' temple at Swarg Ashram/Tapovan near Lakshman Jhula in Rishikesh - NOT the Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga of Nashik, Maharashtra (already documented in this project under trimbakeshwar-temple-nashik), and the name collision is a common source of confusion. The temple is dedicated to Tryambakeshwar, 'the three-eyed lord' (a form of Shiva), but unlike most Shiva temples it houses idols of all Hindu gods and goddesses, with mini-shrines spread across 13 floors. Local tradition says Adi Shankaracharya set it up in the 8th-9th century AD; a travel source claims the 12th century instead (dates conflict - verify). The top floor offers panoramic views of the Ganga and the Himalayan foothills. Sources agree it is a major religious landmark and tourist viewpoint of Rishikesh.

name: Trimbakeshwar Temple
town_description: Rishikesh, the 'Yoga Capital of the World', sits on the Ganges in the foothills of the Himalayas in Uttarakhand, where the river leaves the mountains for the plains. Sacred to Hindus as the place of the sage Raibhya's penance, it is a centre of ashrams, yoga schools and the evening Ganga Aarti, and a gateway to the Char Dham pilgrimage. The suspension bridges Lakshman Jhula and Ram Jhula link the Tapovan and Swarg Ashram temple quarters.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun - about 20-25 km (verify).
travel.railway: Rishikesh Railway Station - about 4-5 km from Lakshman Jhula; Haridwar junction (~25 km) is better connected.
travel.road: On Neelkanth Road near Lakshman Jhula, Tapovan/Swarg Ashram area; reachable by auto-rickshaw and taxi from Rishikesh town and Haridwar.

visitor_information.best_time: October to April for clear weather; Maha Shivaratri and the Shravan month are the most auspicious times to visit.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Approx. 6:00 AM - 12:00 PM and 2:00 PM - 7:00 PM daily per one travel guide (verify locally - no official timings published). No elevators; 13 floors are climbed by stairs.
